page: Vultr vhp-1c-1gb-amd is an entry-level virtual machine instance belonging to the High Performance server family. The configuration includes 1 shared virtual CPU powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The single-core allocation is complemented by 1.0 GB of system memory and 25 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Acceleration hardware is not included, with GPU count fixed at zero, while networking provides 1 complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread execution efficiency paired with overall capacity constraints typical of single-vCPU setups. In stress-ng single-core benchmarks, the AMD EPYC processor attains top-tier performance with a score of 3294.99. Single-threaded data handling remains balanced, yielding 29.37 GB/s in gzip compression and 13.19 GB/s in bzip3 decompression. However, overall multi-core and throughput metrics reflect the 1 vCPU ceiling. PassMark CPU scores evaluate in the lower percentiles at 2738.52, while PassMark memory and database evaluations exhibit constrained bandwidth. Redis SET throughput measures 2.21 million operations per second, and static web serving delivers 1.52 GB/s.

Cost efficiency is centered on providing low-overhead access to modern AMD EPYC microarchitecture and high-speed NVMe storage. Because the single core is shared and total system RAM is limited to 1.0 GB, resource contention can arise during peak usage periods. The server is well matched for utility workloads, lightweight cron processing, low-traffic edge services, development environments, and microservices with minimal memory requirements.
description: Vultr vhp-1c-1gb-amd is an entry-level compute instance providing 1 shared AMD EPYC vCPU clocked at 2.0 GHz, 1.0 GB of RAM, and 25 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 processor includes AVX-512 vector support and achieves top-tier single-core compute results in stress-ng evaluations. However, aggregate system throughput is constrained by the single-core allocation and 1.0 GB memory footprint, as evidenced by lower-tier rankings in multi-core metrics, PassMark database operations, and web serving benchmarks. Without dedicated GPUs, this instance is architected for budget-conscious, low-intensity cloud tasks. It delivers cost-effective resource utilization for small background workers, microservice hosting, lightweight proxy handling, and entry-level development environments that do not demand extensive concurrency or memory depth.
